text:
maria: Heads up — since ~06:20 UTC we’re seeing streaming token stalls from several us-west GPU pools. p50 ok, p99 token latency up ~4x and a bunch of rpc deadline errors for long-lived gRPC streams. Posting to loop folks who might see infra or runtime noise.
aj: saw that too, traces show lots of `rpc deadline exceeded` on the same model route. I grabbed a few tcpdumps; a lot of out-of-order segments and retransmit bursts when stalls happen.
ken: I pulled a pcap from one affected host and reproduced. You can see sequences like S1,S3,S2,S4 — very obvious reordering across the flow. Packet arrival timestamps cluster into microbursts.
jun: FYI we rolled NIC FW on the us-west GPU nodes last night (mellanox 21.28.x). ops-bot reported a partial kernel bump earlier today on that pool. Could be correlated.
ops-bot: deploybot: kernel-5.10.82 rolled to us-west-2-gpu-pool-a between 05:50-06:10 UTC (canary -> 50% -> 100%).
maria: timeline fits. Any ideas on root cause? Is this NIC firmware <-> kernel network offload interaction?
aj: likely. My hypothesis: GSO/LRO handing plus ECMP path changes are causing reordering when the device emits large skbs split across multiple segments and packets hit different tor paths.
ken: also found MTU mismatch on one of the racks — hosts at 1500 while the agg switch configured for 9000 in a handful of racks (tor-12 and tor-14). That’ll break large-frame heuristics and can amplify reordering when GSO splits.
jun: confirmed: tor-12 has jumbo enabled, but the NICs in some GPU blades never got the jumbo MTU due to image config drift. We pushed a config last week that missed that subset.
sre-lead: quick canary suggestions: 1) disable GRO/LRO on a small subset of nodes in pool-a to see if reordering stops; 2) if GRO disable helps, test CPU/throughput impact; 3) temporarily increase gRPC streaming deadline (from 60s -> 120s) for affected route to reduce user impact while we triage; 4) run coordinated tcpdump with tcprewrite timestamps.
maria: we already tried disabling GRO on two nodes — p99 token latency dropped ~30% but CPU increased ~6-8% and throughput slightly decreased. So disabling is a mitigation but not ideal for Dedicated SLAs.
aj: another angle: RDMA path. Some of these servers have SR-IOV + RDMA enabled, and when the kernel falls back due to offload misconfig it can present weird ordering at OS level. Check ofed driver versions?
jun: OFED versions differ across hosts. I’ll inventory and paste results in a follow-up.
ken: short-term we can harmonize MTU to 1500 across the rack for the affected nodes (less risky) — that should avoid GSO split mismatches until we roll a proper config.
sre-lead: agree. Plan: 1) roll MTU harmonization on tor-12/tors for affected racks (orchestration ticket created), 2) disable GRO on a small canary group for 4h to confirm behavior, 3) collect full pcap + perf counters, 4) consider NIC FW rollback if kernel FW combo reproducible.
maria: noted. Also ticketing: customer support flagged Dedicated tenants in us-west seeing token stalls; need a comms plan if this persists.
jun: I’ll run an automated check to compare OFED and FW versions across pools and post a matrix here in ~30m.
ken: I’ll schedule the MTU harmonization for a 5-min maintenance window in 30m; will target 4 hosts first.
aj: for follow-up, can we add a short-term gRPC server-side knob to buffer a bit more before deadline to avoid restarting the stream on transient reorders? Might be safer than raising global deadline.
sre-lead: good ask — product okayed a per-route config change earlier; go ahead with a conservative buffer. Ops: coordinate with product for config rollout.
maria: thanks all. Action items recorded: MTU harmonize, GRO canary, collect pcaps, OFED/FW inventory, small per-route stream buffer. Ping me for blockers. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incidentbot: created INC-2025-0427 (Packet-reordering -> streaming stalls) and linked this thread.
ken: quick note — if anyone wants the pcap I uploaded to /nfs/pcaps/1769454321_usw2_gpu_pool_a.pcap, I’ll give access.
maria: grabbing it now. Will update status in the incident doc after initial canary results. :white_check_mark:
